question: Starting with the matrix $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&0\\2&1&3\\3&0&1\end{bmatrix},$$ apply successively the elementary transformations $R_1\leftrightarrow R_3$, $R_2\to R_2-2R_3$, $C_2\to C_2+C_1$ and $C_3\to C_3-C_1$, in the stated order, and determine the matrix obtained after the complete transformation.
explanation:
Successive Matrix Transformations

Initially, $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&0\\2&1&3\\3&0&1\end{bmatrix}$$ Applying $R_1\leftrightarrow R_3$, we obtain $$\begin{bmatrix}3&0&1\\2&1&3\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix}$$ Now apply $R_2\to R_2-2R_3$. Since $R_2=[2,1,3]$ and $2R_3=[2,4,0]$, the new second row is $[0,-3,3]$. Hence the matrix becomes $$\begin{bmatrix}3&0&1\\0&-3&3\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix}$$ Next apply $C_2\to C_2+C_1$. The new second column is $$\begin{bmatrix}0\\-3\\2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3\\0\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\-3\\3\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, the matrix becomes $$\begin{bmatrix}3&3&1\\0&-3&3\\1&3&0\end{bmatrix}$$ Finally, apply $C_3\to C_3-C_1$. The new third column is $$\begin{bmatrix}1\\3\\0\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}3\\0\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-2\\3\\-1\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, after all the stated elementary transformations, the required matrix is $$\begin{bmatrix}3&3&-2\\0&-3&3\\1&3&-1\end{bmatrix}$$.
